disclaimer: Health information is general population-level information based on published air-quality guidance. It is not a medical diagnosis. Actual health risk depends on concentration, exposure duration, individual susceptibility and other factors.

authoritative_sources.name: WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines (2021)
authoritative_sources.note: Health-based recommendations. WHO notes that guideline levels do not represent a concentration below which absolutely no health effect can occur.

authoritative_sources.name: India National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS 2009)
authoritative_sources.publisher: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India
authoritative_sources.note: Statutory ambient air quality standards for industrial, residential, rural, and other areas in India.

pm25.name: Fine Particulate Matter
pm25.description: Inhalable particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter of 2.5 micrometres or smaller, capable of penetrating deep into alveolar regions of the lungs and entering the bloodstream.
pm25.secondary_formation: Forms directly through mechanical wear and combustion, and secondarily in the atmosphere via nucleation and chemical condensation of precursor gases (SO₂, NOₓ, NH₃, VOCs).
health_effects: Respiratory irritation and reduced lung function
Cardiovascular effects and aggravation of pre-existing heart disease
Long-term exposure is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular mortality, chronic respiratory disease, and lung cancer
vulnerable_groups: Persons with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory disease
Outdoor workers with elevated inhalation rates

primary_sources.description: Vehicle exhaust, tyre and brake wear, and diesel engine emissions
Industrial manufacturing, smelting, and processing plants
Thermal power plants, coal and oil combustion
Residential cooking and heating with solid fuels (wood, coal, dung)
Agricultural crop residue burning and forest/waste fires
Construction activities, unpaved road dust, and demolition

pm10.name: Inhalable Coarse Particulate Matter
pm10.description: Inhalable particles with aerodynamic diameter of 10 micrometres or smaller, typically depositing in the upper respiratory tract and trachea.
health_effects: Respiratory tract irritation, coughing, and throat discomfort
Aggravation of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
Long-term exposure is associated with impaired respiratory health and increased respiratory symptoms
vulnerable_groups: Persons with active asthma or respiratory allergies

primary_sources.description: Resuspension of road dust and mechanical abrasion from vehicle traffic
Building construction, excavation, earthmoving, and demolition dust
Extraction, crushing, screening, and handling of aggregate materials
Field tilling, open soil erosion, and wind-blown dust
Industrial and commercial combustion emissions

no2.name: Nitrogen Dioxide
no2.description: A reddish-brown reactive gas produced primarily during high-temperature fuel combustion, serving as a key precursor for ozone and secondary particulate matter.
health_effects: Worsened respiratory symptoms and increased bronchial reactivity in people with asthma
Long-term exposure is associated with increased risk of respiratory infections and childhood asthma development
vulnerable_groups: Individuals with asthma or airway hyper-reactivity
Elderly persons with chronic heart or lung disease

primary_sources.description: Internal combustion engines, particularly diesel vehicles and heavy lorries
Fossil fuel thermal power stations and gas turbines
Industrial boilers, process furnaces, and kiln firing
Construction equipment, diesel locomotives, and marine transport

o3.name: Ground-Level Ozone
o3.description: A secondary pollutant formed not by direct emissions, but through photochemical reactions between precursor gases (nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds) in the presence of sunlight and heat.
o3.secondary_formation: Formed in the troposphere by photochemical oxidation of VOCs and CO catalysed by nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) under ultraviolet solar radiation. Ground-level ozone is not emitted directly by industrial smokestacks or motor vehicles.
health_effects: Airway irritation, coughing, throat dryness, and chest tightness
Temporary reduction in lung function and inflammation of lung tissue
Short-term exposure can aggravate asthma and trigger respiratory hospital admissions
vulnerable_groups: Outdoor workers and physically active individuals
Children playing outdoors during sunny peak hours
Persons with pre-existing asthma or chronic respiratory illness

primary_sources.description: Vehicular NOₓ and unburnt hydrocarbon/VOC emissions reacting photochemically
Industrial paints, chemical solvents, surface coatings, and petroleum refining releasing VOCs
Power plant and industrial burner NOₓ emissions
Natural plant-emitted volatile organics (isoprene, terpenes) reacting with urban NOₓ

so2.name: Sulfur Dioxide
so2.description: A colourless gas with a pungent, irritating odour, released mainly during the combustion of sulfur-bearing fossil fuels such as coal and crude oil.
health_effects: Airway irritation and bronchoconstriction within minutes of exposure
Can worsen respiratory symptoms, especially in susceptible individuals with asthma
High concentration exposure can cause eye irritation and aggravate cardiovascular distress
vulnerable_groups: Asthma patients and individuals with bronchial hyper-responsiveness
Individuals with active chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

primary_sources.description: Coal-fired and heavy fuel-oil electricity generation facilities
Industrial process boilers, furnaces, and chemical firing
Smelting and roasting of sulfide ores (copper, zinc, lead, iron)
Petroleum refining, catalytic cracking, and fuel desulfurization

co.name: Carbon Monoxide
co.description: A colourless, odourless, and tasteless toxic gas produced by the incomplete combustion of carbonaceous fuels.
health_effects: Reduces oxygen delivery to organs and tissues through formation of carboxyhemoglobin (COHb)
At elevated concentrations, causes headache, dizziness, impaired psychomotor skills, and fatigue
Severe acute exposure can result in loss of consciousness, cardiovascular collapse, and acute poisoning
vulnerable_groups: Individuals with coronary artery disease or cardiovascular conditions
Elderly individuals with compromised circulatory function

primary_sources.description: Petrol and diesel motor vehicles operating under rich fuel-air mixture or cold start
Unvented or poorly ventilated biomass cookstoves, fireplaces, and charcoal burners
Foundries, metallurgical processing, blast furnaces, and chemical plants
Smouldering field residue, open waste burning, and wildfires
